# Read in Logghe et al 2025 which has body size data for ~ 4800 arthropod species and makes up the bulk of the GLiTRS trait data set on body size
# Tidy and clean this data frame to prepare it to merge with the PREDICTS trait data sets
```{r}
# Upload logghe et al
logghe <- read_excel(here("data", "Body_Size_data.xlsx"))

# keep only first 8 cols
logghe <- logghe %>% dplyr::select(1:8)

# Make first row the header
colnames(logghe) <- as.character(logghe[1, ])

# drop first row
logghe <- logghe[-1, ] 

# Create a genus and species column
logghe <- logghe %>%
  separate(scientificName, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "drop")

# Combine genus and species to create Best_guess_binomial which I will use to merge 
logghe <- logghe %>% mutate(Best_guess_binomial = str_c(Genus, Species, sep = " "))

# Reorder columns
logghe <- logghe %>% dplyr::select(order, family, Genus, Species, Best_guess_binomial, Trait_Value) %>% 
  rename(Family = family) %>% 
  rename(Order = order)

# Convert to numeric 
logghe$Trait_Value <-  as.numeric(logghe$Trait_Value)
```

# Read and tidy Geoffrey Su's ant trait data
```{r}
# Load the data
trait_ants <- read_excel(here("data", "SuFormacidaeBodyLength-2014-05-23.xlsx"))

# Rename body length average column into something more readable
trait_ants <- trait_ants %>% rename(avg_body_length_mm = "Body.Length..mm...worker..AVG")

# Lets remove those rows with NAs for body length
trait_ants <- trait_ants %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_body_length_mm) & avg_body_length_mm != 0) # 559 rows with no body length data, 2 rows where BL = 0

# Create best_guess_binomial by combining genus and species  
trait_ants <- trait_ants %>% mutate(Best_guess_binomial = str_c(Genus, Species, sep = " "))

# Filter for the cols of interest for merging
trait_ants <- trait_ants %>% dplyr::select(Genus, Best_guess_binomial, avg_body_length_mm)

# Tidy
trait_ants <- trait_ants %>%
  mutate(
    Order = "Hymenoptera",
    Family = "Formicidae"
  ) %>% 
  rename(Trait_Value = avg_body_length_mm) %>%
  separate(Best_guess_binomial, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::select(Order, Family, Genus, Species, Best_guess_binomial, Trait_Value)
# ants ready
```

# Read and tidy Melanie Edgars beetle trait data
```{r}
# Load Melanies beetle trait data
melanie_beetles <- read_excel(here("data", "EdgarBeetleLength-2014-01-09.xlsx"))

# Combine genus and species for merging
melanie_beetles <- melanie_beetles %>% mutate(Best_guess_binomial = str_c(GENUS, SPECIES, sep = " "))

# Calculate average b.length
melanie_beetles <- melanie_beetles %>%
  separate(B.LENGTH, into = c("b_min", "b_max"), sep = "-", fill = "right", remove = FALSE) %>% # fill = "right" allows single values to stay in b_min while b_max becomes NA.
  mutate(
    b_min = as.numeric(trimws(b_min)), # trimws() removes any leading/trailing spaces 
    b_max = as.numeric(trimws(b_max)),
    b.length_avg = if_else(
      is.na(b_max),
      b_min,  # If no range, use the min value
      (b_min + b_max) / 2  # Else if range, compute the average
    ))

# Prepare and tidy beetles
melanie_beetles <- melanie_beetles %>% 
  mutate(Order = "Coleoptera") %>% 
  dplyr::select(Order, FAMILY, GENUS, SPECIES, Best_guess_binomial, b.length_avg) %>% 
  rename(Family = FAMILY) %>% 
  rename(Genus = GENUS) %>% 
  rename(Species = SPECIES) %>% 
  rename(Trait_Value = b.length_avg)
```

# Read and tidy Rachel Tans bee trait data
```{r}
# Load Rachel bee trait data
rachel_bee <- read_excel(here("data", "BeeTraits_P2_RachelTan.xlsx"))

# Create a genus and species column
rachel_bee <- rachel_bee %>%
  separate(CorrectedName, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "drop")

# Filter for columns of interest
rachel_bee <- rachel_bee %>% dplyr::select(HigherTaxon, Family, Genus, Species, CorrectedName, MidRangeBodyLength) %>% drop_na() # drop those sp. with NA for body length

# Remove rows identified as "sp." or inside brackets e.g., (Dialictus) or (Psithyrus) which are subgenera and not a true species name
rachel_bee <- rachel_bee %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(Species, "sp\\.") &         # remove rows with "sp."
    !str_detect(Species, "\\(.*\\)")        # remove rows with anything in brackets
  )

# Rename for merging
rachel_bee <- rachel_bee %>% 
  rename(Best_guess_binomial = CorrectedName) %>% 
  rename(Order = HigherTaxon) %>% 
  rename(Trait_Value = MidRangeBodyLength)

```

# Merge Logghe, Geoffrey, Melanies and Rachels trait datasets to have an overall body size trait dataset
```{r}
# merge all trait datasets
all_traits <- bind_rows(logghe, melanie_beetles, rachel_bee, trait_ants)

# There are duplicate species entries
all_traits[duplicated(all_traits["Best_guess_binomial"]) | 
                                  duplicated(all_traits["Best_guess_binomial"], fromLast = TRUE), ] %>%  View()

# Sense check - there are 634 duplicates
all_traits[duplicated(all_traits["Best_guess_binomial"]),] 

# For those species with duplicate entries, calculate an average Trait_Value which is the mean of the duplicate entries
all_traits_clean <- all_traits %>%
  group_by(Best_guess_binomial) %>%
  summarise(
    Trait_Value = mean(Trait_Value, na.rm = TRUE),  # average Trait_Value
    across(.cols = -Trait_Value, .fns = ~ first(.x)),  # for each column, take the first value
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Order, Family, Genus, Species, Best_guess_binomial, Trait_Value)

nrow(all_traits) - nrow(all_traits_clean) # 634

rm(all_traits, logghe, melanie_beetles, rachel_bee, trait_ants)
```

# Read in PREDICTS data 
```{r}
# All insect data effort-corrected and merged
taxon_insects <-  qread("/Users/jusi/Desktop/multi-groups/data/predicts-prepared-whole-database.qs")

# Get rid of rows which aren't resolved to order level
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>% filter(Order != "") # 1056 rows not resolved to order

# Recreate genus and species column as sometimes the best_guess_binomial column has a name in PREDICTS but there is no entry in the genus or species column
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Best_guess_binomial = as.character(Best_guess_binomial)) %>%
  separate(Best_guess_binomial, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "merge", fill = "right")

length(unique(taxon_insects$SS))
```

# Clean and tidy PREDICTS data then merge trait dataset based on taxon resolution
```{r}
# There are entries in the column Taxon_name_entered such as "Lasioglossum sp" - such rows tend not to have an entry in the genus column (i.e. Lasioglossum) due to issues with the col API.
# I realised that these rows were therefore being assigned an average mass value at the family level, rather than the genus level - despite the genus information being available. 
# I will extract the genus information from the Taxon_name_entered column for those rows that do not yet have an entry in genus.
# This will improve the precision of the matched mass data, such that these rows will now be matched at the genus level instead of the family level (as they were beforehand)
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(
    Genus = case_when(
      is.na(Genus) | Genus == "" ~ word(Taxon_name_entered, 1), # Check if Genus is empty or missing, if so, extract the first word from Taxon_name_entered and assign it to genus.
      TRUE ~ Genus # If genus is not empty, leave it as the pre-existing genus entry. 
    ))

# Have a look
taxon_insects %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Precision_score) %>% View()

# Remove those entries which have a "?" before or after the name of the genus e.g. "?Abalabus" or "Abalabus?"
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "\\?"))

# Remove leading and trailing double quotation marks
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_replace_all(Genus, '^"|"$', ""))

# Remove any numbers 
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "[0-9]"))

# Remove entries with sp at the end
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove(Genus, "(_|\\s)?sp\\.?$"))

# Get species trait values for merging
sp_value <- all_traits_clean %>% dplyr::select(Best_guess_binomial, Trait_Value) 

# First merge Logghe species level data
taxon_insects <- left_join(taxon_insects, sp_value, by = "Best_guess_binomial")

rm(sp_value)

# Calculate average body length for genera
genus_value <- all_traits_clean %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(genus_avg_body_length = mean(Trait_Value, na.rm = TRUE)) # 2381 genus data

# Merge based on genus where best_guess_binomial is empty
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  left_join(genus_value, by = "Genus", suffix = c("", "_genus")) 

rm(genus_value)

# Average body length per family based on species
family_value <- all_traits_clean %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(family_avg_body_length = mean(Trait_Value, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge based on family where genus and species is empty
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  left_join(family_value, by = "Family", suffix = c("", "_family")) 

rm(family_value)

# priority-based fallback assignment where final body length values are selected based on the first non-missing (or non-blank) column in a defined order.
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(final_body_length = coalesce(
    Trait_Value,
    genus_avg_body_length,
    family_avg_body_length
  ))

# How many rows have data based on each level of taxonomic resolution
taxon_insects %>%
  summarise(across(
    c(Trait_Value,
    genus_avg_body_length,
    family_avg_body_length,
    final_body_length),
    list(
      non_NAs = ~sum(!is.na(.))
    )
  ))
```

# Rainford et al 2014 provides min and max body length data for 760 insect families, I will calculate the average body length between the min and the max and then merge those values onto those rows in my data frame that do not yet have a body length value. 

# First lets tidy the data frame 

```{r}
# Upload 
rainford <- read_excel(here("data", "rainford_body_size.xlsx"))

# Make first row the header
colnames(rainford) <- as.character(rainford[1, ])
rainford <- rainford[-1, ] # drop first row

# Extract cols of interest
rainford <- rainford %>% dplyr::select("Order", "Family", "Min (mm)", "Max (mm)") %>% rename(min_bl = "Min (mm)") %>% rename(max_bl = "Max (mm)")

# Drop rows with all NAs
rainford <- rainford %>%
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))

# Convert cols to numeric
rainford$min_bl <- as.numeric(rainford$min_bl) # Odonata (Pseudolestidae) has an NA for BL hence the warning message
rainford$max_bl <- as.numeric(rainford$max_bl)

# Drop rows only to Order level
rainford <- rainford %>%
  filter(!is.na(Family))

# Calculate average body length
rainford <- rainford %>%
  mutate(Rainford_family_avg = (min_bl + max_bl) / 2)
         
# Simplify for merging
rainford <- rainford %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(-min_bl, -max_bl, -Order))
```

# Merge family average body length from Rainford for those rows in my data frame that do not yet have a body length value

```{r}
# Step 1: Filter rows in taxon_insects where there is no body size value at the species, genus or family level and therefore we can merge a family body size value from Rainford
needs_family_avg <- taxon_insects %>%
  filter(is.na(Trait_Value) & is.na(genus_avg_body_length) & is.na(family_avg_body_length))

# Step 2: Join family_avg body size values from Rainford based on Family column
needs_family_avg <- needs_family_avg %>%
  left_join(rainford, dplyr::select(Family, Rainford_family_avg), by = "Family")

# Step 3: Combine updated rows (need_family_avg) back into original data (taxon_insects)

# First, remove the rows you updated from taxon_insects
remaining_rows <- taxon_insects %>%
  filter(!(is.na(Trait_Value) & is.na(genus_avg_body_length) & is.na(family_avg_body_length)))

# sense check remaining rows should be taxon_insects - needs_family_avg
nrow(taxon_insects) - nrow(needs_family_avg)

# Bind the updated rows with the remaining rows
taxon_insects_updated <- bind_rows(remaining_rows, needs_family_avg)

# How many rows still without a family average
sum(!is.na(taxon_insects_updated$Rainford_family_avg)) # 134120

# How many rows have data based on each level of taxonomic resolution
taxon_insects_updated %>%
  summarise(across(
    c(Trait_Value,
    genus_avg_body_length,
    family_avg_body_length,
    final_body_length,
    Rainford_family_avg),
    list(
      non_NAs = ~sum(!is.na(.))
    )
  ))

rm(needs_family_avg, remaining_rows, taxon_insects)
```

# Now that we have merged all the trait data,  I will coalesce the family average body length values from Rainford into the final_body_length column (for those rows that didn't previously have a body length value at the family level) - if they had already been assigned a body length value at the family level from Logghe or any of the PREDICTS trait datasets - then we will stick with this value.

```{r}
# Coalesce those rows with missing values in final_body_length with the corresponding family_avg
taxon_insects_updated <- taxon_insects_updated %>%
  mutate(final_body_length = coalesce(final_body_length, Rainford_family_avg)) # coalesce(a,b) returns a if its not NA otherwise it returns b

# How many rows do we still not have a body size value for and are still NA - 69814
taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(is.na(Trait_Value) & is.na(genus_avg_body_length) & is.na(family_avg_body_length) & is.na(final_body_length) & is.na(Rainford_family_avg)) %>%
  nrow()

# Have a look at the rows
taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(is.na(Trait_Value) & is.na(genus_avg_body_length) & is.na(family_avg_body_length) & is.na(final_body_length) & is.na(Rainford_family_avg)) %>% 
  View()

# Filter out rows which still don't have a body size value
all_insects_size <- taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(!is.na(final_body_length)) %>% # 1195212
  droplevels()

```

# Sohlstrom et al 2018 has tropical and temperate allometries for different insect orders since the scaling between mass and length differs significantly between either realm. We will therefore split sites in PREDICTS based on their latitude into either tropical or temperate realms.

```{r}
# Add a new column classifying each site into tropical or temperate
all_insects_size$climate_zone <- ifelse(all_insects_size$Latitude >= -23.4368 & all_insects_size$Latitude <= 23.4368, 
                          "tropical", 
                          "temperate")
```

# Read in allometry coefficients
```{r}
coefficients <- read_excel(here("data", "allometry_coefficients.xlsx"))
```

# Merge allometry coefficients to size data
```{r}
# Step 1: Join by order and climate_zone
all_insects_size <- all_insects_size %>%
  left_join(coefficients, by = c("Order", "climate_zone"))

# Step 2: For those taxa in PREDICTS which are not in the big five orders, we will assign them the allometries for all insects
fallback <- coefficients %>%
  filter(Order == "All_insects") %>%
  dplyr::select(climate_zone, a_fallback = a, b_fallback = b)

# Step 3: Join allometries for All_insects based on whether its a tropical or temperate site
all_insects_size <- all_insects_size %>%
  left_join(fallback, by = "climate_zone") %>%
  mutate(
    a = if_else(is.na(a), a_fallback, a), # if a is NA, assign it a for all_insects, else keep it as its order specific a
    b = if_else(is.na(b), b_fallback, b)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-a_fallback, -b_fallback)

# Have a look
all_insects_size %>% dplyr::select(SSBS, Order, final_body_length, Latitude, climate_zone, a, b) %>% unique() %>%  View()
```

# Calculate mass in mg using allometric specific coefficients for each order
```{r}
AllInsectsSize <- all_insects_size %>%
  mutate(
    log10_mass = a + b * log10(final_body_length),
    mass_mg = 10^log10_mass
  )

summary(all_insects_size$final_body_length) # no zero values for final_body_length as min is 0.6
any(all_insects_size$final_body_length == 0) # FALSE

rm(coefficients, fallback, rainford, all_insects_size, all_traits_clean, taxon_insects_updated)
```


# Now we have a data frame with a mass value for all the insect records in PREDICTS. There are many more species level entities in PREDICTS than just filtering based on Best_guess_binomial or the Species column, this is because as mentioned earlier there are many rows in the Taxon_name_entered column such as "Lasioglossum sp" which are species level entities but would be dropped out if I filtered for species level entities using Best_guess_binomial or the Species column (as I did previously). AP has sent an updated taxon resolution file with all of the species level entities in PREDICTS, I will use this file to filter my data frame for all species level entities as my analysis will be at the species level. 

```{r}
# Lets have a look at those rows in Taxon_name_entered that are likely a species level entity
AllInsectsSize %>%
  filter(str_detect(Taxon_name_entered, regex("sp\\.|cf|aff|[0-9]", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% 
dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Family, Genus, Species, Trait_Value, genus_avg_body_length, family_avg_body_length, final_body_length, log10_mass) %>% View()

# Filter for columns of interest
AllInsectsSizeFiltered <- AllInsectsSize %>% dplyr::select(Source_ID, SS, SSB, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, log10_mass, Diversity_metric, Diversity_metric_unit, Merged_diversity, Predominant_habitat, Use_intensity)

# Filter for diversity metrics of interest - abundance and occurrence data can be used
AllInsectsSizeFiltered <- AllInsectsSizeFiltered %>% filter(Diversity_metric %in% c("abundance", "effort-corrected abundance", "density", "group abundance", "occurrence", "occurrence frequency", "relative abundance"))

# Load taxon resolution file
TaxonResolution <- readRDS(here("data", "CuratedTaxonResolution2.rds"))

# Step 1: Filter TaxonResolution for species-level entries - i.e. those entries with a precision score of 4!
TaxonResolutionSp <- TaxonResolution %>%
  filter(PrecisionScore == 4) %>%
  dplyr::select(SS, Taxon_name_entered) # select cols for merging

# Step 2: Keep only matching rows in AllInsectsSizeFiltered
OnlySpecies <- AllInsectsSizeFiltered %>%
  semi_join(TaxonResolutionSp, by = c("SS", "Taxon_name_entered")) # keeps only rows in AllInsectsSizeFiltered that have a match in TaxonResolutionSp. based on SS and Taxon_name_entered

# OnlySpecies now contains only the rows from AllInsectsSizeFiltered that correspond to species-level entries in TaxonResolutionSp. 

# Lets have a look at those rows which have an entry for Taxon_name_entered but no entry for Best_guess_binomial!
OnlySpecies %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Taxon_name_entered) & Taxon_name_entered != "",
    is.na(Best_guess_binomial) | Best_guess_binomial == ""
  ) %>% View()

# Create a present or absent column - its present if Merged_diversity > 0 and absent if its 0
OnlySpecies <- OnlySpecies %>%
  mutate(PresentOrAbsent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0, 1, 0))

# Create a log(abundance when present) column
OnlySpecies <- OnlySpecies %>% 
  mutate(
    LogAbundanceWhenPresent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0,
                                    log(Merged_diversity),
                                    NA))

# Have a look at how many rows are present versus absent
table(OnlySpecies$PresentOrAbsent)

OnlySpecies %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, PresentOrAbsent, Merged_diversity, LogAbundanceWhenPresent) %>% View()


# Rename predominant habitat since its not really habitat we're looking at
OnlySpecies <- rename(OnlySpecies,
                Predominant_land_use = Predominant_habitat)

# Relevel the land use and use intensity classes
OnlySpecies <- OnlySpecies %>%
  mutate(
    # collapse primary forest and non-forest together into primary vegetation as these aren't well distinguished
    Predominant_land_use = recode_factor(Predominant_land_use, 
                                         "Primary forest" = "Primary", 
                                         "Primary non-forest" = "Primary"),
    # indeterminate secondary veg and cannot decide get NA
   Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Secondary vegetation (indeterminate age)"),
    Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Cannot decide"), 
    Use_intensity = na_if(Use_intensity, "Cannot decide"),
    
    # set reference levels
    Predominant_land_use = factor(Predominant_land_use),
    Predominant_land_use = relevel(Predominant_land_use, ref = "Primary"),
    Use_intensity = factor(Use_intensity),
    Use_intensity = relevel(Use_intensity, ref = "Minimal use")
  )

table(OnlySpecies$Predominant_land_use)
table(OnlySpecies$Predominant_land_use, OnlySpecies$Use_intensity)
```

# Following Charlie and Tims analysis, I will collapse LU categories into Primary, Secondary vegetation, Low-intensity agriculture and high-intensity agriculture so that we have a manageable number of coefficients to analyse. 

```{r}

OnlySpecies <- OnlySpecies %>%
  mutate(
    LandUseFinal = case_when(
      # Primary stays as is
      Predominant_land_use == "Primary" ~ "Primary",

      # Any secondary vegetation type -> Secondary Vegetation
      Predominant_land_use %in% c("Young secondary vegetation",
                                  "Intermediate secondary vegetation",
                                  "Mature secondary vegetation") ~ "Secondary vegetation",

      # Plantation forest depends on intensity
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity == "Minimal use" ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity %in% c("Light use", "Intense use") ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Pasture
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Cropland
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Drop Urban by assigning NA -these will get dropped when we create the model data
      Predominant_land_use == "Urban" ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Turn into factor if you want ordered categories
  mutate(LandUseFinal = factor(LandUseFinal,
                               levels = c("Primary", "Secondary vegetation",
                                          "Low-intensity agriculture", "High-intensity agriculture")))

table(OnlySpecies$LandUseFinal)
```

# Create random intercept for Species

```{r}
OnlySpecies <- OnlySpecies %>%
  mutate(
    SpeciesFinal = case_when(
      Species != "" & !is.na(Species) ~ Species, # If species is present, use that as the random intercept
      (Species == "" | is.na(Species)) & Best_guess_binomial != "" & !is.na(Best_guess_binomial) ~ Best_guess_binomial, # If species is blank, use BGB as the random intercept
      (Species == "" | is.na(Species)) & (Best_guess_binomial == "" | is.na(Best_guess_binomial)) ~ paste(SS, Taxon_name_entered, sep = " "),
      # If Species and BGB is blank, use SS and Taxon_name_entered combined as the random intercept
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Lets have a look 
OnlySpecies %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Best_guess_binomial, Species, Taxon_name_entered, SpeciesFinal) %>% View()


sum(is.na(OnlySpecies$SpeciesFinal))
OnlySpecies %>% filter(SpeciesFinal == "")
sum(is.na(OnlySpecies$SpeciesFinal) | OnlySpecies$SpeciesFinal == "")


length(unique(OnlySpecies$SpeciesFinal))
length(unique(OnlySpecies$Taxon_name_entered))
length(unique(OnlySpecies$Best_guess_binomial))
length(unique(OnlySpecies$Species))
```

# Create model data

```{r}
# drop all rows with NAs for variables of interest
ModelDataSizeOccurrence <- drop_na(OnlySpecies, LandUseFinal, Use_intensity, PresentOrAbsent) %>% droplevels()
ModelDataSizeAbundance <- drop_na(OnlySpecies, LandUseFinal, Use_intensity, LogAbundanceWhenPresent) %>% droplevels()

length(unique(ModelDataSizeAbundance$SS)) # 389 studies 
length(unique(ModelDataSizeAbundance$SSBS)) # 8896 sites
```

#### Load in model plot function

```{r}
## Load in a model criticism function - this function is used for checking the residual/model diagnostic plots to test that the model is meeting all of its assumptions
model_plot <-function(mod.for.plot){
  require(lattice)
  
  # set up a 2 x 2 grid for plotting
  par(mfrow = c(2,2))
  par(ask = TRUE)
  
  # qqplot
  qqnorm(resid(mod.for.plot))
  qqline(resid(mod.for.plot), col = 2)
  
  # residuals vs fitted plot
  plot(fitted(mod.for.plot), resid(mod.for.plot),xlab = "Fitted Values", ylab = "Residuals", main = "Residuals vs fitted")
  abline(h=0, lty=2)
  lines(smooth.spline(fitted(mod.for.plot), resid(mod.for.plot)), col = "red")
  
  # histogram of residuals
  hist(resid(mod.for.plot))
  
  # random effects distribution
  dotplot(ranef(mod.for.plot,condVar = TRUE))
}
```

```{r}
  mutate(

    OccurrenceSE    = OccurrencePredictions$se.fit,
    OccurrenceLwr = OccurrenceFit - 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,
    OccurrenceUpr = OccurrenceFit + 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,

    OccurrenceProb   = plogis(OccurrenceFit), # predicted probability - plogis() is the inverse of the logit function.
    # It takes values on the logit (link) scale (from −∞ to +∞) and transforms them into probabilities between 0 and 1.
    LowerProb = plogis(OccurrenceLwr), # 95% CI lower bound
    UpperProb = plogis(OccurrenceUpr) # 95% CI upper bound
```

# The occurrence plots show us how likely is the taxa to be present and the abundance plots show us the predicted abundance when the taxa is present. If I multiply the predictions from both plots together - that gives me the predicted abundance of a taxa without knowing in advance whether it is present or not. I will multiply the predictions and calculate the combined standard errors to achieve this. 

# I tried two methods for combining the predictions/standard errors from the occurrence and abundance models. 

# (OLD CODE) - The first was to multiply the fits and use a formula to calculate the standard errors, see below. However the predictions are on different scales. The occcurrence predictions are on the logit link scale, which requires plogis() to backtransform them to get probabilities and the abundance predictions are on the log scale which requires exp() to get abundance counts. Multiply them together would be fitofboth = fit_link * fit_abundance OR logit(probability) * log(abundance) - there's no standard inverse for this and the multiplication of different link scales is not equivalent to multiplying probabilities with counts. See the next chunk for the correct method.

```{r}
# Combine data frames and calculate product and SE
NewDataCombined <- NewDataOccurrenceMass %>%
  bind_cols(NewDataAbundanceMass %>% 
              dplyr::select(fit_abund = fit,
                     se_abund  = se)) %>%
  mutate(
    # product of predictions
    FitOfBoth = fit_link * fit_abund,
    
    # standard error of product (assuming independence)
    SEofBoth  = sqrt((fit_link^2) * (se_abund^2) +
                       (fit_abund^2) * (se_link^2) +
                       (se_link^2) * (se_abund^2)),
    # 95% confidence intervals
    LowerOfBoth = FitOfBoth - 1.96 * SEofBoth,
    UpperOfBoth = FitOfBoth + 1.96 * SEofBoth
  )
  
```


# If my desired outcome is the predicted abundance when accounting for probability of occurrence, it makes more sense to backtransform each prediction to its natural scale first, such that occurrence_prob = plogis(fit_link) and abund_exp = exp(fit_abund). This would lead to occurrence_prob being the probability of occurrence and abund_exp being the predicted abundance. I would then multiply these two components such that pred_abundance = occ_prob * abund_exp and use the delta method to calculate the SEs. 

```{r}
# Backtransform and calculate predicted abundance with CIs
NewDataCombined <- NewDataOccurrenceMass %>%
  bind_cols(NewDataAbundanceMass %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                pred_backtransformed = pred_backtransformed,
                     se_log10  = se_log10)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Probability of occurrence * predicted abundance when present = predicted abundance 
    PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability = OccurrenceProb * pred_backtransformed,  # c = a * b
    # Delta method
    occurrence_var  = (OccurrenceProb * (1 - OccurrenceProb))^2 * (OccurrenceSE^2), # variance of plogis(fit_link)
    abundance_var = (log(10)^2) * (pred_backtransformed^2) * (se_log10^2), # variance of 10^(fit_abund)

    combined_var =
      (pred_backtransformed^2) * occurrence_var +
      (OccurrenceProb^2) * abundance_var,

    predictedcombinedvar = sqrt(combined_var),

    # 95% CIs on original (abundance) scale
    predictedcombinedlwr =
      PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability -
      1.96 * predictedcombinedvar,
    predictedcombinedupr =
      PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability +
      1.96 * predictedcombinedvar
  )
    
  
# Plot
FinalPlotAbundanceOccurrenceMassCombined <- ggplot(NewDataCombined,
       aes(x = 10^log10_mass, y = PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability,
           color = LandUseFinal, fill = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = predictedcombinedlwr, ymax = predictedcombinedupr),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  labs(x = "Body mass (mg)",
       y = "Predicted abundance = a x b (± 95 % CI)",
       color = "Land use") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal()


#ggsave(filename = "./figures/c4_updated/BodyMassAbundanceOccurrenceCombined.png",  plot = FinalPlotAbundanceOccurrenceMassCombined, width = 6, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

# Read in PREDICTS data and ensure that species level entities such as "Lasioglossum sp." in the Taxon_name_entered column are assigned a genus level egg size value. 

```{r}
# All insect data effort-corrected and merged
taxon_insects <-  qread("/Users/jusi/Desktop/multi-groups/data/predicts-prepared-whole-database.qs")

# Get rid of rows which aren't resolved to order level
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>% filter(Order != "") # 1056 rows not resolved to order

# Recreate genus and species column as sometimes BGB is present in PREDICTS but no info for genus or sp.
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Best_guess_binomial = as.character(Best_guess_binomial)) %>%
  separate(Best_guess_binomial, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "merge", fill = "right")

# There are entries in PREDICTS such as "Lasioglossum sp" - rows with such names tend to not have an entry in the genus column (due to issues with the COL API)
# Previously these taxa were getting family level values in the average mass analysis, despite their genus information being available.
# I will extract the genus information from the Taxon_name_entered column for those rows that do not yet have an entry in genus.
# This will improve the precision of the matching, such that these rows will now be matched at the genus level instead of the family level (as they were beforehand)
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(
    Genus = case_when(
      is.na(Genus) | Genus == "" ~ word(Taxon_name_entered, 1), # Check if Genus is empty or missing, if so, extract the first word from Taxon_name_entered and assign it to genus.
      TRUE ~ Genus # If genus is not empty, leave it as the pre-existing genus entry. 
    ))

# Have a look
taxon_insects %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Precision_score) %>% View()

# Remove those entries which have a "?" before or after the name of the genus e.g. "?Abalabus" or "Abalabus?"
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "\\?"))

# Remove leading and trailing double quotation marks
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_replace_all(Genus, '^"|"$', ""))

# Remove any numbers 
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "[0-9]"))

# Remove entries with sp at the end
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove(Genus, "(_|\\s)?sp\\.?$"))

# Filter for columns of interest
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>% dplyr::select(Source_ID, SS, SSB, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Diversity_metric, Diversity_metric_unit, Merged_diversity, Predominant_habitat, Use_intensity)
```

# Start merging egg volume data with PREDICTS

```{r}
# helper: returns the value if all the same, otherwise NA - this sets an NA for log10Vol for those rows with duplicate species entries
all_same_or_na <- function(x) {
  if (length(unique(na.omit(x))) == 1) unique(na.omit(x)) else NA
}

# Calculate mean egg volume for those taxa with duplicate entries
EggDataNoDuplicates <- egg_data %>%
  group_by(Best_guess_binomial, drop = FALSE) %>% # don't drop rows with NA for BGB, i.e. those rows with genus egg size values
  summarise(
    Volume_mm3 = mean(Volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(-Volume_mm3, all_same_or_na),
    .groups = "drop") 

# Get species trait values for merging
sp_value <- EggDataNoDuplicates %>% dplyr::select(Best_guess_binomial, Volume_mm3) 

# First merge species level data
taxon_insects <- left_join(taxon_insects, sp_value, by = "Best_guess_binomial")

rm(sp_value)

# Number of species matched
taxon_insects %>%
  filter(!is.na(Volume_mm3)) %>% 
  group_by(Order) %>%
  summarise(n_species = n_distinct(Best_guess_binomial)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_species))  

# Calculate average egg volume for genera
genus_value <- EggDataNoDuplicates %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3 = mean(Volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE)) # 3322 genus data

# Merge based on genus where best_guess_binomial is empty
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  left_join(genus_value, by = "Genus", suffix = c("", "_genus")) 

# Average egg volume per family based on species values
family_value <- EggDataNoDuplicates %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3 = mean(Volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge based on family where genus and species is empty
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  left_join(family_value, by = "Family", suffix = c("", "_family")) 

# priority-based fallback assignment where final egg volume values are selected based on the first non-missing (or non-blank) column in a defined order.
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3 = coalesce(
    Volume_mm3,
    GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3,
    FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3
  ))

# How many rows have data based on each level of taxonomic resolution
taxon_insects %>%
  summarise(across(
    c(Volume_mm3,
    GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3,
    FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3,
    FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3),
    list(
      non_NAs = ~sum(!is.na(.))
    )
  ))
```

# There are some rows in the egg volume dataset which give an egg volume value for the name of a genus rather than a species (i.e. a full binomial). I have already matched egg volume values using the species values, the average of species within the same genus and the average of genera within the same family. I will now extract the egg volume values for those rows in the dataset which are ONLY for genera. I will then merge the egg volume values for those genera to taxa in PREDICTS which do not currently have a genus level egg volume value, I will then do the same for those rows resolved to family (i.e. calculate the average egg volume for the family based on the egg volume data JUST for genera)

# First lets have a look at those rows which are just values for genera..

```{r}
# Which rows are egg volume values for taxa with both a genus and a species name, i.e. a full binomial
with_binomial <- egg_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Best_guess_binomial)) %>%
  group_by(Best_guess_binomial) %>%
  summarise(
    Volume_mm3 = mean(Volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(-Volume_mm3, all_same_or_na),
    .groups = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::select(Order, Family, Binomial_Name, Best_guess_binomial, Genus, Species, Volume_mm3, log10Vol)

# Filter for rows that do not have a species name and are therefore egg volume values for genera
without_binomial <- egg_data %>%
  filter(is.na(Best_guess_binomial))

# Which genera have I not already used in the previous chunk to match to species in predicts (i.e. are not in the with_binomial df) and therefore will be useful to match to taxa in PREDICTS without an egg volume value already..
UsefulGenera <- without_binomial %>%
  anti_join(with_binomial, by = "Genus") 
```

# I will now match those egg volume values for genera which I have not yet matched to taxa in PREDICTS (because the value was only for the name of a genus rather than a full latin binomial)
# I will do this only for those taxa in PREDICTS which do not yet have an egg volume value at the species, genus or family level (that is if they already have an egg volume value at the species level, there would be no point assigning a genus or family level value)..

```{r}
# First lets calculate the mean egg volume for duplicate genus entries 
UsefulGeneraNoDuplicates <- UsefulGenera %>%
  group_by(Genus, drop = FALSE) %>% # don't drop NAs, i.e. those rows with genus egg size values
  summarise(
    GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3 = mean(Volume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(-Volume_mm3, all_same_or_na),
    .groups = "drop") %>% 
  dplyr::select(Order, Family, Binomial_Name, Best_guess_binomial, Genus, Species, GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3, log10Vol)

# Simplify for merging
DiffGenusAvg <- UsefulGeneraNoDuplicates %>% 
  dplyr::select(Genus, GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3)

# Step 1: Filter rows in test without an egg volume value at the species, genus or family level and therefore require an egg volume value
NeedsValue <- taxon_insects %>%
  filter(is.na(Volume_mm3) & is.na(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3))

# Step 2: Join genus egg volume values for those genera we have not captured yet
NeedsValue <- NeedsValue %>%
  dplyr::select(-GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3) %>%   # drop old column to avoid duplicate
  left_join(DiffGenusAvg, by = "Genus")

# Average egg volume for families
DiffFamilyAvg <- UsefulGeneraNoDuplicates %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3 = mean(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge based on family where genus and species is empty
NeedsValue <- NeedsValue %>%
  dplyr::select(-FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3) %>% 
  left_join(DiffFamilyAvg, by = "Family", suffix = c("", "_family")) 

# Combine updated rows (NeedsValue) back into original data (taxon_insects)
# First, remove the rows you updated from test
remaining_rows <- taxon_insects %>%
  filter(!(is.na(Volume_mm3) & is.na(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3)))

# sense check remaining_rows should be taxon_insects - NeedsValue
nrow(taxon_insects) - nrow(NeedsValue)

# Bind them together
taxon_insects_updated <- bind_rows(remaining_rows, NeedsValue)

# How many rows still without a family average
sum(is.na(taxon_insects_updated$FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3)) # 167353
sum(is.na(taxon_insects$FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3)) # 178615

# 178615 - 167353 = 11262 rows which got a family value from the additional genera
```

# Now that we have merged all the egg volume data, coalesce the additional genus and family averages into the FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3 column

```{r}
# Replace those rows with missing values in FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3 with the corresponding FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3
taxon_insects_updated <- taxon_insects_updated %>%
  mutate(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3 = coalesce(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3, FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3)) # coalesce(a,b) returns a if its not NA otherwise it returns b

# How many rows do we still not have a egg volume value for and are still NA - 153284
taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(is.na(Volume_mm3) & is.na(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3)) %>%
  nrow()

# Have a look at those rows
taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(is.na(Volume_mm3) & is.na(GenusAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FamilyAvgEggVolume_mm3) & is.na(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3)) %>%
  View()

# Filter out rows which still don't have a egg volume value
AllInsectsEggSize <- taxon_insects_updated %>%
  filter(!is.na(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3)) %>% 
  droplevels()

rm(DiffFamilyAvg, DiffGenusAvg, family_value, genus_value, NeedsValue, remaining_rows, UsefulGenera, UsefulGeneraNoDuplicates, with_binomial, without_binomial,
   EggDataNoDuplicates, egg_data, taxon_insects_updated, taxon_insects)
```

# Now that I have an overall data frame for egg size for all insect taxa in PREDICTS, I will now filter it for species level entities using APs taxon resolution file and then prepare the data frame for analysis.

```{r}
# Filter for diversity metrics of interest - abundance and occurrence data can be used (i.e. no species richness data)
AllInsectsEggSize <- AllInsectsEggSize %>% filter(Diversity_metric %in% c("abundance", "effort-corrected abundance", "density", "group abundance", "occurrence", "occurrence frequency", "relative abundance"))

# Load taxon resolution file
TaxonResolution <- readRDS(here("data", "CuratedTaxonResolution2.rds"))

# Step 1: Filter TaxonResolution for species-level entries - i.e. those entries with a precision score of 4!
TaxonResolutionSp <- TaxonResolution %>%
  filter(PrecisionScore == 4) %>%
  dplyr::select(SS, Taxon_name_entered) # select cols for merging

# Step 2: Keep only matching rows in AllInsectsEggSize
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSize %>%
  semi_join(TaxonResolutionSp, by = c("SS", "Taxon_name_entered")) # keeps only rows in AllInsectsEggSize that have a match in TaxonResolutionSp. based on SS and Taxon_name_entered

# AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly now contains only the rows from AllInsectsEggSize that correspond to species-level entries in TaxonResolutionSp. 

# Lets have a look at those rows which have an entry for Taxon_name_entered but no entry for Best_guess_binomial!
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Taxon_name_entered) & Taxon_name_entered != "",
    is.na(Best_guess_binomial) | Best_guess_binomial == ""
  ) %>% View()

# Create a present or absent column - its present if Merged_diversity > 0 and absent if its 0
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(PresentOrAbsent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0, 1, 0))

# Create a log(abundance when present) column
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>% 
  mutate(
    LogAbundanceWhenPresent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0,
                                    log(Merged_diversity),
                                    NA))

# Create a log(egg size) column
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>% 
  mutate(
    LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 = log(FinalAvgEggVolume_mm3))


# Have a look at how many rows are present versus absent
table(AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly$PresentOrAbsent)

# Rename predominant habitat since its not really habitat we're looking at
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- rename(AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly,
                Predominant_land_use = Predominant_habitat)

# Relevel the land use and use intensity classes
AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(
    # collapse primary forest and non-forest together into primary vegetation as these aren't well distinguished
    Predominant_land_use = recode_factor(Predominant_land_use, 
                                         "Primary forest" = "Primary", 
                                         "Primary non-forest" = "Primary"),
    # indeterminate secondary veg and cannot decide get NA
   Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Secondary vegetation (indeterminate age)"),
    Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Cannot decide"), 
    Use_intensity = na_if(Use_intensity, "Cannot decide"),
    
    # set reference levels
    Predominant_land_use = factor(Predominant_land_use),
    Predominant_land_use = relevel(Predominant_land_use, ref = "Primary"),
    Use_intensity = factor(Use_intensity),
    Use_intensity = relevel(Use_intensity, ref = "Minimal use")
  )

table(AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly$Predominant_land_use)
table(AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly$Predominant_land_use, AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly$Use_intensity)
```

# Recode the land use classes to have Primary, Secondary vegetation, Low-intensity agriculture and high-intensity agriculture

```{r}

AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(
    LandUseFinal = case_when(
      # Primary stays as is
      Predominant_land_use == "Primary" ~ "Primary",

      # Any secondary vegetation type -> Secondary Vegetation
      Predominant_land_use %in% c("Young secondary vegetation",
                                  "Intermediate secondary vegetation",
                                  "Mature secondary vegetation") ~ "Secondary vegetation",

      # Plantation forest depends on intensity
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity == "Minimal use" ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity %in% c("Light use", "Intense use") ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Pasture
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Cropland
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Drop Urban by assigning NA -these will get dropped when we create the model data
      Predominant_land_use == "Urban" ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Turn into factor if you want ordered categories
  mutate(LandUseFinal = factor(LandUseFinal,
                               levels = c("Primary", "Secondary vegetation",
                                          "Low-intensity agriculture", "High-intensity agriculture")))

table(AllInsectsEggSizeSpeciesOnly$LandUseFinal)
```

# Modelling log(abundance of present species) ~ LUFinal * Egg Size

```{r}
# basic data diagnostics
str(ModelDataEggAbundance)
table(ModelDataEggAbundance$LandUseFinal, useNA="ifany")
n_distinct(ModelDataEggAbundance$Source_ID)
n_distinct(ModelDataEggAbundance$SS)
n_distinct(ModelDataEggAbundance$SpeciesFinal)

# Convert to factors
ModelDataEggAbundance$Order <- as.factor(ModelDataEggAbundance$Order)
ModelDataEggAbundance$Family <- as.factor(ModelDataEggAbundance$Family)
ModelDataEggAbundance$SpeciesFinal <- as.factor(ModelDataEggAbundance$SpeciesFinal)
ModelDataEggAbundance$SS <- as.factor(ModelDataEggAbundance$SS)
ModelDataEggAbundance$SSB <- as.factor(ModelDataEggAbundance$SSB)
```

# Maximal random effects structure

```{r}
ab_m1 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Drop block
ab_m2 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID/SS) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Drop SS
ab_m3 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))


# Drop Family
ab_m4 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID) + (1 | SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Compare models
anova(ab_m1, ab_m2, ab_m3, ab_m4)  # Likelihood ratio test
AIC(ab_m1, ab_m2, ab_m3, ab_m4)


# ab_m1 best!
```

# Backwards stepwise selection of fixed effects

```{r}
# Additive model with the interaction removed but both predictors still present
ab_m5 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal + LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))


# Just land use as predictor
ab_m6 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal + (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Just egg as the predictor
ab_m7 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 + (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Make a null, intercept only model
ab_m8 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), data = ModelDataEggAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))


## Compare the models
AIC(ab_m1, ab_m5, ab_m6, ab_m7, ab_m8)
anova(ab_m1, ab_m5, ab_m6, ab_m7, ab_m8)
anova(ab_m7, ab_m5, ab_m1)
```

# Interaction model only marginally better (p = 0.046) than additive model. AIC difference small, only 2 points.  
# Generate predictions from the model

```{r}
# Create a grid of values
NewDataAbundanceEggSize <- expand.grid(
  LogAvgEggVolume_mm3 = seq(from = min(ModelDataEggAbundance$LogAvgEggVolume_mm3),
                   to = max(ModelDataEggAbundance$LogAvgEggVolume_mm3),
                   length.out = 100),
  LandUseFinal = levels(ModelDataEggAbundance$LandUseFinal))
  

# Get predictions without random effects, with SEs
AbundancePredictions <- predict(ab_m1, newdata = NewDataAbundanceEggSize, re.form = NA, se.fit = TRUE)

# Predictions on log scale
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$pred_log <- AbundancePredictions$fit
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$se_log   <- AbundancePredictions$se.fit

# 95% CI on log scale
value <- qnorm(0.975)
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$log_lwr <- NewDataAbundanceEggSize$pred_log -
                                  value * NewDataAbundanceEggSize$se_log
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$log_upr <- NewDataAbundanceEggSize$pred_log +
                                  value * NewDataAbundanceEggSize$se_log

# Back-transform all of them
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$pred_backtransformed <- exp(NewDataAbundanceEggSize$pred_log)
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$lwr_backtransformed <- exp(NewDataAbundanceEggSize$log_lwr)
NewDataAbundanceEggSize$upr_backtransformed  <- exp(NewDataAbundanceEggSize$log_upr)


# Extract coefficient in primary
fixef(ab_m1)["LogAvgEggVolume_mm3"]

# Significance of body mass effect in primary
bayestestR::convert_pd_to_p(parameters::p_value(ab_m1, method = "eti"))

# Extract mass x land use F ratio
anova(ab_m1)
Anova(ab_m1)

# Create a back-transformed egg volume column for plotting
NewDataAbundanceEggSize <- NewDataAbundanceEggSize %>%
  mutate(EggVolume_mm3 = exp(LogAvgEggVolume_mm3))

# Plot
PlotAbundanceEggSize <- ggplot(NewDataAbundanceEggSize,
       aes(x = EggVolume_mm3, y = pred_backtransformed,
           color = LandUseFinal, fill = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr_backtransformed, ymax = upr_backtransformed),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(
    labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  labs(x = expression("Egg volume (mm"^3*")"),
       y = "Abundance of present species (± 95 % CI)",
       color = "Land use") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal()



# Remove legend
PlotAbundanceEggSizeNoLegend <- PlotAbundanceEggSize + theme(legend.position = "none")

# Add text box
```

# The interactive model is the best fit, go ahead and generate predictions and create the plot. 

```{r}
# Interaction more significant that just additive effect of mass
anova(oc_m1)

# Create new data frame for predictions
NewDataOccurrenceEggSize <- expand.grid(
  ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3 = seq(from = min(ModelDataEggOccurrence$ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE),
                to   = max(ModelDataEggOccurrence$ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100),
  LandUseFinal = levels(ModelDataEggAbundance$LandUseFinal))

# Copy the factor levels from the model data
NewDataOccurrenceEggSize$LandUseFinal <- factor(NewDataOccurrenceEggSize$LandUseFinal, 
                              levels = levels(ModelDataEggOccurrence$LandUseFinal))

# Predicted probabilities on link scale (logit) with SE
OccurrencePredictions <- predict(oc_m1, newdata = NewDataOccurrenceEggSize, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE, re.form = NA)
       
# Add predictions into data frame
NewDataOccurrenceEggSize <- NewDataOccurrenceEggSize %>%
  mutate(
    OccurrenceFit   = OccurrencePredictions$fit,
    OccurrenceSE    = OccurrencePredictions$se.fit,
    OccurrenceLwr = OccurrenceFit - 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,
    OccurrenceUpr = OccurrenceFit + 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,
    # Back-transform to probability scale
    OccurrenceProb   = plogis(OccurrenceFit), # predicted probability - plogis() is the inverse of the logit function.
    # It takes values on the logit (link) scale (from −∞ to +∞) and transforms them into probabilities between 0 and 1.
    LowerProb = plogis(OccurrenceLwr), # 95% CI lower bound
    UpperProb = plogis(OccurrenceUpr) # 95% CI upper bound
  )

# Extract coefficient in primary
fixef(oc_m1)["ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3"]

# Significance of body mass effect in primary
bayestestR::convert_pd_to_p(parameters::p_value(oc_m1, method = "eti"))

# Extract mass x land use F ratio
anova(oc_m1)
Anova(oc_m1)

# Extract mean and sd from scaled variable to backtransform

log_sd   <- attr(ModelDataEggOccurrence$ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3, "scaled:scale")

# Add a new column with the back transformed values:
NewDataOccurrenceEggSize$BackTransformedEggVolume_mm3 <- exp(NewDataOccurrenceEggSize$ScaledLogAvgEggVolume_mm3 * log_sd + log_mean)

# Plot
PlotOccurrenceEggSize <- ggplot(NewDataOccurrenceEggSize,
       aes(x = BackTransformedEggVolume_mm3, y = OccurrenceProb,
           color = LandUseFinal, fill = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
```

# If my desired outcome is the predicted abundance when accounting for probability of occurrence, it makes more sense to backtransform each prediction to its natural scale first, such that occurrence_prob = plogis(fit_link) and abund_exp = exp(fit_abund). This would lead to occurrence_prob being the probability of occurrence and abund_exp being the predicted abundance. I would then multiply these two components such that pred_abundance = occ_prob * abund_exp and use the delta method to calculate the SEs. 

```{r}
# Backtransform and calculate predicted abundance with CIs
NewDataCombined <- NewDataOccurrenceEggSize %>%
  bind_cols(NewDataAbundanceEggSize %>% 
              dplyr::select(
                pred_backtransformed = pred_backtransformed,
                     se_log  = se_log)) %>%
  mutate(
    # Probability of occurrence * predicted abundance when present = predicted abundance 
    PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability = OccurrenceProb * pred_backtransformed,  # c = a * b
    # Delta method
    occurrence_var  = (OccurrenceProb * (1 - OccurrenceProb))^2 * (OccurrenceSE^2), # variance of plogis(fit_link)
    abundance_var = (pred_backtransformed^2) * (se_log^2), # variance of exp(fit_abund)

    combined_var =
      (pred_backtransformed^2) * occurrence_var +
      (OccurrenceProb^2) * abundance_var,

    predictedcombinedvar = sqrt(combined_var),

    # 95% CIs on original (abundance) scale
    predictedcombinedlwr =
      PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability -
      1.96 * predictedcombinedvar,
    predictedcombinedupr =
      PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability +
      1.96 * predictedcombinedvar
  )
    
  
# Plot
FinalPlotAbundanceOccurrenceEggSizeCombined <- ggplot(NewDataCombined,
       aes(x = BackTransformedEggVolume_mm3, y = PredictedAbundanceAccountingForOccurrenceProbability,
           color = LandUseFinal, fill = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = predictedcombinedlwr, ymax = predictedcombinedupr),
              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  labs(x = expression("Egg volume (mm"^3*")"),
       y = "Predicted abundance = a x b (± 95 % CI)",
       color = "Land use") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal()

#ggsave(filename = "./figures/c4_updated/EggSizeAbundanceOccurrenceCombined.png",  plot = FinalPlotAbundanceOccurrenceEggSizeCombined, width = 6, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

# Calculate average trophic level based on LARVAL diet

```{r}
larvae_diet <- traits %>% dplyr::select(c(1:8, 33:40))

# define diet columns for filtering
LarvalDiets <- c("Larval diet | Fungivory",                                     
                    "Larval diet | Detritivory",                                  
                    "Larval diet | Phytophagy",                                    
                    "Larval diet | Predation",                                    
                    "Larval diet | Parasitoidism",                                 
                    "Larval diet | Ecto-parasitism",                              
                    "Larval diet | Non-feeding",
                    "Larval diet | Liquid feeding and nectivory")

# filter for taxa where the larval diet is not an NA and has a fuzzy coding > 0 - i.e. that diet is present!
larvae_diet <- larvae_diet %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(LarvalDiets), ~ !is.na(.) & . > 0)) 

# Filter for big five
BigFiveLarvalDiet <- larvae_diet %>% filter(Order %in% c("Coleoptera", "Diptera", "Hemiptera", "Hymenoptera", "Lepidoptera"))

# Map trophic levels onto larval diet categories
trophic_map <- c(
  "Larval diet | Fungivory" = 2,
  "Larval diet | Detritivory" = 2,
  "Larval diet | Phytophagy" = 2,
  "Larval diet | Predation" = 3,
  "Larval diet | Parasitoidism" = 3,
  "Larval diet | Ecto-parasitism" = 3,
  "Larval diet | Non-feeding" = NA,   # But there are no larval diets which are non feeding
  "Larval diet | Liquid feeding and nectivory" = 2.5
)

# Pivot longer to have each row a larval diet category across families
BigFiveLarvalDiet_long <- BigFiveLarvalDiet %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Larval diet"),
    names_to = "Diet",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(TrophicLevel = trophic_map[Diet])

# Weighted mean trophic level per family
AverageLarvalTrophicLevelFamily <- BigFiveLarvalDiet_long %>%
  filter(!is.na(TrophicLevel)) %>%
  mutate(
    Value = as.numeric(Value),
    TrophicLevel = as.numeric(TrophicLevel)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Family) %>%
  summarise(
    AvgTrophicLevel = weighted.mean(TrophicLevel, Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

# Read in PREDICTS data and ensure that species level entities such as "Lasioglossum sp." are included for merging average trophic level values using the Taxon_name_entered column

```{r}
# All insect data effort-corrected and merged
taxon_insects <-  qread("/Users/jusi/Desktop/multi-groups/data/predicts-prepared-whole-database.qs")

# Get rid of rows which aren't resolved to order level
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>% filter(Order != "") # 1056 rows not resolved to order

# Recreate genus and species column as sometimes BGB is present in PREDICTS but no info for genus or sp.
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Best_guess_binomial = as.character(Best_guess_binomial)) %>%
  separate(Best_guess_binomial, into = c("Genus", "Species"), sep = " ", remove = FALSE, extra = "merge", fill = "right")

# There are entries in PREDICTS such as "Lasioglossum sp" - rows with such names tend to not have an entry in the genus column (due to issues with the COL API)
# Previously these taxa were getting family level values in the average mass analysis, despite their genus information being available.
# I will extract the genus information from the Taxon_name_entered column for those rows that do not yet have an entry in genus.
# This will improve the precision of the matching, such that these rows will now be matched at the genus level instead of the family level (as they were beforehand)
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(
    Genus = case_when(
      is.na(Genus) | Genus == "" ~ word(Taxon_name_entered, 1), # Check if Genus is empty or missing, if so, extract the first word from Taxon_name_entered and assign it to genus.
      TRUE ~ Genus # If genus is not empty, leave it as the pre-existing genus entry. 
    ))

# Have a look
taxon_insects %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Precision_score) %>% View()

# Remove those entries which have a "?" before or after the name of the genus e.g. "?Abalabus" or "Abalabus?"
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "\\?"))

# Remove leading and trailing double quotation marks
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_replace_all(Genus, '^"|"$', ""))

# Remove any numbers 
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove_all(Genus, "[0-9]"))

# Remove entries with sp at the end
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>%
  mutate(Genus = str_remove(Genus, "(_|\\s)?sp\\.?$"))

# Filter for columns of interest
taxon_insects <- taxon_insects %>% dplyr::select(Source_ID, SS, SSB, SSBS, Order, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, Best_guess_binomial, Diversity_metric, Diversity_metric_unit, Merged_diversity, Predominant_habitat, Use_intensity)
```

```{r}
  )

# Have a look at an example family where we have the average trophic level for the adult but not for the larvae
AllInsectsTrophicLevel %>% dplyr::select(SS, SSBS, Family, Genus, Species, Taxon_name_entered, AvgTrophicLevel_larval, AvgTrophicLevelAdult) %>% 
  filter(Family == "Acartophthalmidae") %>% View()

rm(AverageAdultLarvaeTrophicLevelFamily, taxon_insects)
```

# Now that I have an overall data frame for average trophic level for all insect taxa in PREDICTS, I will now filter it for species level entities using APs taxon resolution file and then prepare the data frame for analysis.

```{r}
# Filter for diversity metrics of interest - abundance and occurrence data can be used (i.e. no species richness data)
AllInsectsTrophicLevel <- AllInsectsTrophicLevel %>% filter(Diversity_metric %in% c("abundance", "effort-corrected abundance", "density", "group abundance", "occurrence", "occurrence frequency", "relative abundance"))

# Load taxon resolution file
TaxonResolution <- readRDS(here("data", "CuratedTaxonResolution2.rds"))

# Step 1: Filter TaxonResolution for species-level entries - i.e. those entries with a precision score of 4!
TaxonResolutionSp <- TaxonResolution %>%
  filter(PrecisionScore == 4) %>%
  dplyr::select(SS, Taxon_name_entered) # select cols for merging

# Step 2: Keep only matching rows in AllInsectsTrophicLevel
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevel %>%
  semi_join(TaxonResolutionSp, by = c("SS", "Taxon_name_entered")) # keeps only rows in AllInsectsTrophicLevel that have a match in TaxonResolutionSp. based on SS and Taxon_name_entered

# AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly now contains only the rows from AllInsectsTrophicLevel that correspond to species-level entries in TaxonResolutionSp. 

# Create a present or absent column - its present if Merged_diversity > 0 and absent if its 0
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(PresentOrAbsent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0, 1, 0))

# Create a log(abundance when present) column
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>% 
  mutate(
    LogAbundanceWhenPresent = ifelse(Merged_diversity > 0,
                                    log(Merged_diversity),
                                    NA))

# Have a look at how many rows are present versus absent
table(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$PresentOrAbsent)

# Rename predominant habitat since its not really habitat we're looking at
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- rename(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly,
                Predominant_land_use = Predominant_habitat)

# Relevel the land use and use intensity classes
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(
    # collapse primary forest and non-forest together into primary vegetation as these aren't well distinguished
    Predominant_land_use = recode_factor(Predominant_land_use, 
                                         "Primary forest" = "Primary", 
                                         "Primary non-forest" = "Primary"),
    # indeterminate secondary veg and cannot decide get NA
   Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Secondary vegetation (indeterminate age)"),
    Predominant_land_use = na_if(Predominant_land_use, "Cannot decide"), 
    Use_intensity = na_if(Use_intensity, "Cannot decide"),
    
    # set reference levels
    Predominant_land_use = factor(Predominant_land_use),
    Predominant_land_use = relevel(Predominant_land_use, ref = "Primary"),
    Use_intensity = factor(Use_intensity),
    Use_intensity = relevel(Use_intensity, ref = "Minimal use")
  )

table(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Predominant_land_use)
table(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Predominant_land_use, AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Use_intensity)
```

# Recode the land use classes to have Primary, Secondary vegetation, Low-intensity agriculture and high-intensity agriculture

```{r}

AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(
    LandUseFinal = case_when(
      # Primary stays as is
      Predominant_land_use == "Primary" ~ "Primary",

      # Any secondary vegetation type -> Secondary Vegetation
      Predominant_land_use %in% c("Young secondary vegetation",
                                  "Intermediate secondary vegetation",
                                  "Mature secondary vegetation") ~ "Secondary vegetation",

      # Plantation forest depends on intensity
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity == "Minimal use" ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Plantation forest" & Use_intensity %in% c("Light use", "Intense use") ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Pasture
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Pasture" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Cropland
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity %in% c("Minimal use", "Light use") ~ "Low-intensity agriculture",
      Predominant_land_use == "Cropland" & Use_intensity == "Intense use" ~ "High-intensity agriculture",

      # Drop Urban by assigning NA -these will get dropped when we create the model data
      Predominant_land_use == "Urban" ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  # Turn into factor if you want ordered categories
  mutate(LandUseFinal = factor(LandUseFinal,
                               levels = c("Primary", "Secondary vegetation",
                                          "Low-intensity agriculture", "High-intensity agriculture")))

table(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$LandUseFinal)
```

# Create random intercept for Species

```{r}
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly <- AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>%
  mutate(
    SpeciesFinal = case_when(
      Species != "" & !is.na(Species) ~ Species,
      (Species == "" | is.na(Species)) & Best_guess_binomial != "" & !is.na(Best_guess_binomial) ~ Best_guess_binomial,
      (Species == "" | is.na(Species)) & (Best_guess_binomial == "" | is.na(Best_guess_binomial)) ~ paste(SS, Taxon_name_entered, sep = " "),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

sum(is.na(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$SpeciesFinal))
AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly %>% filter(SpeciesFinal == "")
sum(is.na(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$SpeciesFinal) | AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$SpeciesFinal == "")


length(unique(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$SpeciesFinal))
length(unique(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Taxon_name_entered))
length(unique(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Best_guess_binomial))
length(unique(AllInsectsTrophicLevelSpeciesOnly$Species))
```

# Modelling log(abundance of present species) ~ LUFinal * average LARVAL trophic level

```{r}
# Maximal random effects structure
ab_m1 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * AvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | Source_ID/SS/SSB) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Drop block
ab_m2 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * AvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | Source_ID/SS) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Drop SS
ab_m3 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * AvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | Source_ID) + (1| Family/SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Drop Family
ab_m4 <- blmer(LogAbundanceWhenPresent ~ LandUseFinal * AvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | Source_ID) + (1 | SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance,
                   control = lme4::lmerControl(
                     optimizer = "nloptwrap",
                     optCtrl = list(algorithm = "NLOPT_LN_SBPLX", maxeval = 1e6)))

# Compare models
anova(ab_m1, ab_m2, ab_m3, ab_m4)  # Likelihood ratio test
AIC(ab_m1, ab_m2, ab_m3, ab_m4)


# ab_m1 best!
```

```{r}
## Compare the models
```

# Generate predictions from the model

```{r}
# Create a grid of values
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae <- expand.grid(
  AvgTrophicLevel_larval = seq(from = min(ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance$AvgTrophicLevel_larval),
                   to = max(ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance$AvgTrophicLevel_larval),
                   length.out = 100),
  LandUseFinal = levels(ModelDataLarvalDietAbundance$LandUseFinal))
  

# Get predictions without random effects, with SEs
AbundancePredictions <- predict(ab_m1, newdata = NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae, re.form = NA, se.fit = TRUE)

# Add predictions and 95% CIs
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundFit <- AbundancePredictions$fit
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundSE  <- AbundancePredictions$se.fit
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$ExpAbundFit <- exp(NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundFit)  # back-transform
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundLwr <- exp(NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundFit - 1.96 * NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundSE) # exponentiate log abundance values 
NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundUpr <- exp(NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundFit + 1.96 * NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae$AbundSE)

summary(ab_m1)

# Extract coefficient in primary
fixef(ab_m1)["AvgTrophicLevel_larval"]

# Significance of body mass effect in primary
bayestestR::convert_pd_to_p( parameters::p_value(ab_m1, method = "eti"))

# Extract mass x land use F ratio
anova(ab_m1)
Anova(ab_m1)

# Plot
PlotAbundanceTrophicLarvae <- ggplot(NewDataAbundanceTrophicLarvae, aes(x = AvgTrophicLevel_larval, y = ExpAbundFit,
                   color = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = AbundLwr, ymax = AbundUpr, fill = LandUseFinal), alpha = 0.2, color = NA, show.legend = F) +
  labs(x = expression("Larval trophic level"),
       y = "Abundance of present species (± 95 % CI)",
       color = "Land use") +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2,3), labels = c("Primary consumer", "Secondary consumer")) 


# Remove legend for plot for combining later
PlotAbundanceTrophicLarvaeNoLegend <- PlotAbundanceTrophicLarvae + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2,3), labels = c("PC", "SC"))

# Add text
FinalPlotAbundanceTrophicLarvaeNoLegend <-  ggdraw(PlotAbundanceTrophicLarvaeNoLegend) +
  draw_label("Coefficient in primary: 
  - 0.13 [95% CI: -0.24, -0.02], p = 0.02
              Larval TL x LU interaction: 
  F-ratio = 5.04, p = 0.002", x = 0.96, y = 0.96, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.9, size = 10)

# Singular plot to save on its own (not combining later)
FinalPlotAbundanceTrophicLarvae <- ggdraw(PlotAbundanceTrophicLarvae) +
```

# Random effects structure
```{r}
# Just run the model on its own

               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(

                 optCtrl = list(maxfun = 7e5)))

# Save the model
#saveRDS(oc_m1, file = "LarvalTrophicLevelOccurrenceModel.rds")

# Put model formulas in a list
RandomEffectsModelCalls <- list(
  oc_m1 = quote(
    bglmer(PresentOrAbsent ~ LandUseFinal * ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | SS) + (1| SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(
                 optimizer = "Nelder_Mead",
                 optCtrl = list(maxfun = 7e5)
  ))
  ),
  oc_m2 = quote(
    bglmer(PresentOrAbsent ~ LandUseFinal * ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | SS), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(
                 optimizer = "Nelder_Mead",
                 optCtrl = list(maxfun = 7e5)
  ))
  ))

# Run models in parallel
RandomEffectsResults <- mclapply(RandomEffectsModelCalls, function(expr) eval(expr),
                                 mc.cores = 2)

oc_m1 <- RandomEffectsResults[[1]]

anova(oc_m1, oc_m2)  # Likelihood ratio test
```

```{r}
# Additive model
FixedEffectsModelCalls <- list(
  oc_m3 = quote(
    bglmer(PresentOrAbsent ~ LandUseFinal + ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | SS) + (1| SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(

               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(
                 optimizer = "Nelder_Mead",
                 optCtrl = list(maxfun = 7e5)
  ))
  ),
  # Just average trophic level as a predictor
  oc_m5 = quote(
    bglmer(PresentOrAbsent ~ ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval + (1 | SS) + (1| SpeciesFinal), 
               data = ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence, family = binomial(link = "logit"),
               control = lme4::glmerControl(
                 optimizer = "Nelder_Mead",
                 optCtrl = list(maxfun = 7e5)
  ))
  ),
  # Make a null, intercept only model
  oc_m6 = quote(

               control = lme4::glmerControl(

# Run models in parallel
```

```{r}
# Interaction more significant that just additive effect of trophic level
anova(oc_m1)

# Create new data frame for predictions
NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae <- expand.grid(
  ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval = seq(from = min(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval, na.rm = TRUE),
                to   = max(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval, na.rm = TRUE),
                length.out = 100),
  LandUseFinal = levels(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$LandUseFinal))

# Copy the factor levels from the model data
NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae$LandUseFinal <- factor(NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae$LandUseFinal, 
                              levels = levels(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$LandUseFinal))

# Predicted probabilities on link scale (logit) with SE
OccurrencePredictions <- predict(oc_m1, newdata = NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE, re.form = NA)
       
 # Add predictions into data frame
NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae <- NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae %>%
  mutate(
    OccurrenceFit   = OccurrencePredictions$fit,
    OccurrenceSE    = OccurrencePredictions$se.fit,
    OccurrenceLwr = OccurrenceFit - 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,
    OccurrenceUpr = OccurrenceFit + 1.96 * OccurrenceSE,
    # Back-transform to probability scale
    OccurrenceProb = plogis(OccurrenceFit), # predicted probability
    LowerProb = plogis(OccurrenceLwr), # 95% CI lower bound
    UpperProb = plogis(OccurrenceUpr) # 95% CI upper bound
  )

# Extract coefficient in primary
fixef(oc_m1)["ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval"]

# Significance of body mass effect in primary
bayestestR::convert_pd_to_p(parameters::p_value(oc_m1, method = "eti"))

# Extract mass x land use F ratio
anova(oc_m1)
Anova(oc_m1)

# Extract the mean and sd to add the unscaled values back into the prediction data frame for plotting
mean_val <- attr(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval, "scaled:center")
sd_val   <- attr(ModelDataLarvalDietOccurrence$ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval, "scaled:scale")

# Add a new column with the back transformed values:
NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae$UnscaledAvgTrophicLevel <- NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae$ScaledAvgTrophicLevel_larval * sd_val + mean_val

PlotOccurrenceTrophicLarvae <- ggplot(NewDataOccurrenceTrophicLarvae, aes(x = UnscaledAvgTrophicLevel, y = OccurrenceProb, color = LandUseFinal, fill = LandUseFinal)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +

              alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +

       y = "Probability of occurrence (± 95 % CI)",
       color = "Land use",
       fill = "Land use") +

# Remove legend

  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2,3), labels = c("PC", "SC"))

# Add text box 
FinalPlotOccurrenceTrophicLarvaeNoLegend <- ggdraw(PlotOccurrenceTrophicLarvaeNoLegend) +
  draw_label("Coefficient in primary: 
   - 0.04 [95% CI: -0.07, -0.02], p < 0.001
              Larval TL x LU interaction: 
  F-ratio = 23.72, p < 0.0001", x = 0.96, y = 0.96, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 0.9, size = 10)

# Final singular plot
FinalPlotOccurrenceTrophicLarvae <- ggdraw(PlotOccurrenceTrophicLarvae) +
  draw_label("Coefficient in primary: 
   - 0.04 [95% CI: -0.07, -0.02], p < 0.001
              Larval TL x LU interaction:
```
